title: Long exact sequence for cohomology with support
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme, let
$i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed subscheme with open complement
$j:U\hookrightarrow X$, and let $F$ be a
torsion etale sheaf on the
small etale site of $X$. In the
notation of [def-pur-support-cohomology], there is a long exact
sequence

$$
\cdots\longrightarrow H^q_Z(X,F)\longrightarrow H^q(X,F)
\longrightarrow H^q(U,F)\longrightarrow H^{q+1}_Z(X,F)\longrightarrow\cdots,
$$

functorial in the pair $(X,X\setminus Z)$ and in $F$. The same
statement holds for bounded-below complexes with torsion cohomology in the
derived category of [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], and on the
pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] of $X$ for finite-torsion coefficients.
(Source: Milne, Lectures on Etale Cohomology, Section 9, Theorem 9.4;
the bounded-below and pro-etale extensions follow from the site argument below.)

external.place: (Source: Milne, Lectures on Etale Cohomology, Section 9, Theorem 9.3 and the exactness axiom of the etale site.) Step 1: the derived support object.

proof.text: Apply the normalized derived boundary theorem lem-pur-derived-injective-boundary to the three additive functors: the kernel of restriction, evaluation on the terminal object, and evaluation on the open object. Their composite inclusion and restriction is zero by the kernel equation. This constructs boundary natural transformations on the entire bounded-below derived category and fixes their value on every injective representative by the right-derived-unit comparisons.

For etale abelian sheaves, the open-complement arrow is monic because its underlying scheme map is an open immersion. Injective restriction is surjective by lem-weil-pbc-injective-sheaf-mono-restriction. Hence the kernel-inclusion/restriction sequence is short exact termwise on any injective complex. The three exactness assertions of the complex homology sequence, transported through the canonical model isomorphisms, prove SupportSequenceExact. Restrict the boundary transformations to the full subcategory of torsion coefficients.

For each commuting square of pairs and each quantified adjoint chain map, naturality of that chain map and the pair square give a morphism of the two restriction maps on section complexes. The target support inclusion is a kernel, so it gives a unique support chain map. Apply the naturality of the long exact sequence to the resulting morphism of short exact complexes. Normalization of the two derived boundary transformations identifies this boundary square with exactly SupportSequencePairNatural, for every injective representative and every displayed representative isomorphism.

Repeat in sheaves valued in modules over the specified universe lift of A_{E,n}, without forgetting scalars or changing the site. To prove injective restriction surjectivity directly, the free module presheaves on the lifted representables of W and V have a monic map induced by W to V: postcomposition is injective and the free-module basis map is injective. Sheafification is exact, so the underlying presheaf of an injective sheaf is injective (by the sheafification adjunction). Extend the section map from the first free presheaf to the second by injectivity; evaluating on id_V gives an extension of the original section over W. The same kernel, homology exactness, and pair-naturality arguments then prove the pro-etale factor for all of its module coefficients. No etale/pro-etale comparison, scalar-forgetting comparison, or descent hypothesis is used. The coefficient-twist unit module def-coefficient-twists-detailed remains imported to preserve the fixed unit route; the support construction itself is independent of twisting.

sequence

$$
\cdots\longrightarrow H^q_Z(X,F)\longrightarrow H^q(X,F)
\longrightarrow H^q(U,F)\longrightarrow H^{q+1}_Z(X,F)\longrightarrow\cdots,
$$

functorial in the pair $(X,X\setminus Z)$ and in $F$. The same
statement holds for bounded-below complexes with torsion cohomology in the

proof.text:
Step 1: the derived support object. For a bounded-below complex $F$ (a torsion sheaf placed in degree zero) and
$I^{\bullet}$ a K-injective resolution, the complex of sections with
support in $Z$ is the kernel of the restriction
$\Gamma(X,I^{\bullet})\to\Gamma(U,I^{\bullet})$, which is exact, and the
kernel is the complex computing $R\Gamma_Z(X,\cdot)$ by
[def-pur-support-cohomology]. Step 2: the exactness axiom. For a
torsion sheaf $F$ the sequence of presheaves
$0\to\Gamma_Z(V,F)\to\Gamma(V,F)\to\Gamma(V\cap U,F)\to0$ is exact for
every open $V$ of the finite-type scheme $X$: a section $f$ of
$F$ on $V\cap U$ need not extend, but for the sheaf $F$ the exact
sequence $0\to j_!j^*F\to F\to i_*i^*F\to0$ is exact (the open and
closed counterpart of the recollement, the standard exactness of
support and restriction on the (pro-)etale site,
[def-weil-open-closed-recollement]) and its global-sections
sequence is the sequence of the statement. Step 3: the long exact
sequence. The short exact sequence of complexes

$$
0\longrightarrow\Gamma_Z(X,I^{\bullet})
\longrightarrow\Gamma(X,I^{\bullet})
\longrightarrow\Gamma(U,I^{\bullet})\longrightarrow0
$$

(the exactness at the last arrow holding because $I^{\bullet}$ is
K-injective, hence flabby on the (pro-)etale site: the restriction map
of a flabby resolution is surjective, by Step 2 applied to an
injective resolution and the flabbiness of injective sheaves on a
site) gives, by the zig-zag/snake lemma applied to the exact sequence
of cochain complexes, the long exact sequence of cohomology

$$
\cdots\to H^q_Z(X,F)\to H^q(X,F)\to H^q(U,F)\to H^{q+1}_Z(X,F)\to\cdots,
$$

with the connecting morphism the one of the K-injective
resolution; the functoriality in the pair and in $F$ is the
functoriality of all the maps. Step 4: complexes and the pro-etale
site. For bounded-below complexes with torsion cohomology the same
argument runs with a K-injective resolution (the exactness of the
level (2) sequence for each term and the five-lemma over the
spectral sequence of the double complex), and the finite-torsion case
on the pro-etale site is the transport of the etale statement along
the site comparison [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] of the proper-base-change chapter (the sheaves being finite-torsion, the site comparison preserves
the support and the exactness).
